what: Live Nation is the largest live music company in the world. It promotes concerts and festivals, owns or books hundreds of venues, manages artists, and owns Ticketmaster, which sells the tickets.
customers: Concert-goers, artists and their managers, venues, and sponsors.
money: the largest part of revenue, thin margin
brand sponsorship of tours, festivals and venues
moat: Control of all three sides at once: the artists, the venues and the ticketing, so each side reinforces the others.
risks: The US Department of Justice has sued to break up the company over Ticketmaster
Ticketing fees attract political and regulatory attention worldwide
Net margin is around 2% because concert promotion itself barely makes money
opportunities: Revenue grew about 9% last year and about 15% a year over three years
Demand for live events has stayed strong across price points
New stadium and amphitheatre projects raise high-margin venue revenue
watch: Concert attendance, ticketing volumes, and the antitrust case.
